answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost.
